text: dsh-code-index 是面向 DSH 的本地代码索引与上下文工具插件，适合在维护现有代码库时查找符号、理解模块关系并评估变更影响。它将代码扫描和符号索引接入 DSH 工具面，并可把有界仓库地图注入系统提示。主要能力包括符号搜索与引用追踪、仓库结构地图、按任务挑选源码上下文，以及从 Git 改动推导调用方、导入依赖和候选测试；Impact X-Ray 以交互视图展示这些关系和来源证据。适合希望让编码 agent 更快定位代码并检查改动周边影响的开发者。索引和分析在本地工作区进行，不需要额外 API Key；安装要求 Node.js 22 或更高版本。

dsh-code-index adds local code indexing to DSH. Developers can search symbols, trace references, inspect repository maps, gather task context, and review likely callers, imports, and test leads for Git changes. Impact X-Ray shows source relationships. It requires no API key and needs Node.js 22+.

dsh-code-index 的功能「符号搜索」：按符号名称或片段搜索仓库索引，返回匹配结果及文件行号，便于定位定义。通过 DSH 的 code_search 工具触发。
dsh-code-index 的功能「变更影响上下文」：分析 Git diff 或指定文件、符号，列出变更符号、调用方、导入依赖、影响路径和可能相关的测试。通过 code_change_context 工具触发。
dsh-code-index 的功能「任务源码上下文」：用自然语言描述代码任务，工具选择相关符号、文件、调用关系和测试，并在字符预算内提供源码片段及纳入理由。通过 code_context 工具触发。
dsh-code-index 的功能「Impact X-Ray 关系视图」：将变更分析结果呈现为有界的交互图，展示调用、导入、测试线索和可查看的源码证据。通过 code_change_context 请求 xray 输出。

dsh-code-index README · Impact X-Ray：**See the blast radius before your AI edits the code.**

A local [DeepSeek Harness (DSH)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugin that turns a code diff into an inspectable map of potentially affected callers, imports and test leads. Click a relationship to check its source file, line and evidence.

**For DSH users working with existing code:** inspect likely ripple effects before asking an AI agent to edit. Install the stable **v0.11.2** in a compatible DSH profile:

dsh-code-index README · Impact X-Ray：Restart Desktop after installation. v0.11.2 allows DSH `>=0.2.0-rc.2`, including prereleases, without an upper bound. rc.5 passed host compatibility checks, plugin loading and basic ToolRuntime calls; full Desktop UI and model-driven Agent validation are not claimed. Future versions may load but have not all been verified. [Install details](#install) · [v0.11.2 release](https://github.com/lemonxiny55/dsh-code-index/releases/tag/v0.11.2).

dsh-code-index README · Impact X-Ray：**Watch the 30-second real Desktop demo:** a change to `normalize()` → inspect callers and a test lead → click a relationship to see the actual source location.

[Watch MP4](assets/impact-xray-mvp.mp4) · [Full-size GIF](assets/impact-xray-mvp.gif) · [Demo notes and reproduction](assets/impact-xray-mvp-demo.md) · [Install v0.11.2 from npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-code-index/v/0.11.2) · [Project](https://github.com/lemonxiny55/dsh-code-index)

It shows existing analysis and source evidence; it is not a model-driven Agent latency or success claim. See [recording provenance](assets/impact-xray-mvp-demo.md).

dsh-code-index README · Impact X-Ray：- Start from a Git diff or an explicitly selected file/symbol; inspect callers, import dependents, paths and candidate tests.
- Click a relationship to inspect its provenance and available source snapshot at a file and line.
- Treat candidates as leads: `name-only` matches can be uncertain, and a test lead does not prove coverage or failure.

dsh-code-index README · Impact X-Ray：Impact X-Ray is an interactive view of the existing `code_change_context` analysis and source reader; it does not add an impact-analysis engine. Relationships are static evidence, not guaranteed runtime impact.

dsh-code-index README · Impact X-Ray：**Verified:** full X-Ray UI in Desktop 0.2.1-rc.2; Web/Host rc.3 verified for all eight tools and X-Ray (no model-driven Agent run). Desktop 0.2.0-rc.2 passed installation and ToolRuntime checks, not full X-Ray UI. Keep each host's first-party packages on the same declared version. [v0.11.1 evidence and limits](RELEASE_EVIDENCE_v0.11.1.md).

Ask the Agent to call `code_change_context` with:

```json
{"repoRoot":"/absolute/path/to/repo","outputFormat":"xray"}
```

dsh-code-index README · Impact X-Ray：Expand the tool result, choose **Expand view**, and select an arrow. The UI follows the host language and also offers English / 简体中文. Call graph, import graph, test leads, impact paths and gaps each have their own tab. Depth/confidence filters and local expansion only reveal the bounded snapshot; they do not fetch more analysis.

dsh-code-index README · Impact X-Ray：| Relationship | Display | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `exact` | Solid | Structurally resolved under the existing index; not guaranteed runtime impact |
| `import-scoped` | Dashed | Import-scope evidence, with the original reason retained |

dsh-code-index README · Impact X-Ray：Arrows retain actual caller → callee or importer → module endpoints. Test conventions never become invented function-call arrows. Whole-path confidence retains the weakest relation. Saved source is a snapshot; rerun after edits. Deleted declarations use baseline source when available and do not offer a misleading current-file preview.

dsh-code-index README · Impact X-Ray：The presentation caps at **32 nodes, 48 arrows, 12 paths, 8 test/import leads each**, 900 characters per source window and 96,000 UTF-8 bytes of metadata. Call relationships reserve at most 24 symbol nodes / 32 arrows. Optional X-Ray text caps at 24,000 JS characters; the default canonical text and `code_context` packs remain unchanged. The existing index/reference analysis runs before projection, so these UI caps are not a constant-memory guarantee for large repositories. See the measured costs and host compatibility methods in the [MVP report](IMPACT_XRAY_MVP.md).

dsh-code-index README · Impact X-Ray：Reproduce the real demo without overwriting an existing directory:

```sh
npm run build
node scripts/impact-xray-demo.mjs /absolute/path/to/new-demo-repo
```

The script commits a six-source-file baseline and changes `normalize()` from trimming to uppercase conversion. Its baseline Node test passes; the edited test intentionally fails. `looseUsage` deliberately lacks an import, so its name-only relation remains uncertain.

dsh-code-index README · Impact X-Ray：Give your [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) agent the bounded source context it needs to start a code task. One `code_context` call selects primary declarations, strong callers/callees, imports, current changes, and likely tests, with exact source ranges and reasons for inclusion. When evidence is missing, the pack says so.

dsh-code-index README · Impact X-Ray：- **Source within budget:** complete declarations, then whole-line windows, then explicit signature-only fallback. Overlapping source lines are deduplicated; current and baseline excerpts stay separate.
- **One selected pack:** text and opt-in structured output consume the same final ContextPack. Both stay within the default 5000-character cap.
- **Evidence you can inspect:** inclusion reasons are separate from `exact` / `import-scoped` / `name-only` relationship provenance. No probability or confidence estimate is invented.
- **Local and current:** isolated repo/worktree indexes, external add/change/delete freshness, no external indexing API key. Existing full/compact surfaces and v0.8 configuration remain supported.

dsh-code-index README · Impact X-Ray：Introduced in [v0.10.0](https://github.com/lemonxiny55/dsh-code-index/releases/tag/v0.10.0) and retained in v0.11.0: ArkTS `.ets` files use a dedicated, pinned parser to find component structs, methods, fields and decorators, navigate statically identifiable ETS/TS references, and retrieve actual source in bounded Context Packs. The installed package passed real DSH Desktop Agent verification and Node 22/24 release checks. Partial or failed parses report bounded diagnostics.

dsh-code-index README · Impact X-Ray：This supports syntax and static code context, without full HarmonyOS SDK semantics, HAR/module-alias resolution or state-update/UI rerender graphs. See [release evidence](RELEASE_EVIDENCE_v0.10.0.md), [ArkTS PoC](ARKTS_POC_v0.10.0.md) and [the bilingual announcement](assets/v0.10.0-announcement.md). The v0.9.1 Gitignore directory whitelist fix remains included.

dsh-code-index README · Quick start：Requires Node 22/24. The v0.11.2 allows DSH `>=0.2.0-rc.2`, including prereleases; matching first-party packages should be used. Later versions may attempt to load but have not all been verified. Install into an existing Desktop profile using its bundled `dsh` CLI:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-code-index@0.11.2
```

Restart Desktop after installation. For a matching Web profile:

dsh-code-index README · Quick start：```sh
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.1-rc.2 plugin --profile web add dsh-code-index@0.11.2
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.1-rc.2 web
```

For local development, run `pnpm install` and `pnpm build` at the repository root, then use `plugin --profile web add .`. See [Install](#install) for profile options.

dsh-code-index README · Project isolation and live updates：```text
Open repo A → search finds A's symbols
Switch to repo B → search finds B's symbols, not A's
Edit files outside DSH → the next query sees the change
Switch back to A → A's context is still isolated

Each Git worktree gets its own index and change state. The plugin watches projects accessed by the session and checks file metadata on tool calls, so additions, edits, and deletions become visible without a manual rebuild.

dsh-code-index README · Tools：| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `code_index` | Status / (re)build the index for the current workspace |
| `code_symbols` | List symbols (functions, classes, interfaces, types, methods…) with file:line — filtered by name, path, kind, exported |
| `code_search` | Ranked lookup: exact > prefix > substring > subsequence-fuzzy, exports first, relevance score + file:line |
| `code_map` | Bounded ranked repo map (top files by symbol density + import-graph PageRank, key symbols + lines) |
| `code_refs` | Trace a symbol through the call graph: callers (who calls it) and callees (what it calls), resolved to file:line |
| `code_change_context` | Start from the working-tree or an explicit diff and return changed symbols, callers, import dependents, bounded impact paths, and likely tests |
| `code_context` | Edit-ready ContextPack: bounded source, reasons, relationships, changes/tests, gaps, and a hard budget; text by default |
| `code_health` | Opt-in (`codeHealth: true`): circular dependencies (import cycles) and orphan modules |

dsh-code-index README · Tools：Plus an optional **auto-injected system prompt section** (`code-index:repo-map`, order 60): a compact ranked map selected from the active DSH session workspace. Set `autoInject: false` to disable and rely on the `code_map` tool only.

dsh-code-index README · Install：Requires `dsh` (any install path — npx, npm, or source) and Node ≥ 22.

The v0.11.2 declares `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools: >=0.2.0-rc.2`, with no upper bound. DSH includes prereleases when checking this range, so future DSH versions may attempt to load the plugin; this does not mean every version has been verified. Use matching DSH/dsh-tools groups. The plugin surface remains a preview API, and future releases may introduce incompatibilities.

dsh-code-index README · Install：Desktop checks DSH peer requirements before activation. v0.10.0's exact `0.2.0-rc.2` pin is rejected by DSH `0.2.1-rc.2`; v0.10.1 enumerated the then-supported groups; v0.11.2 removes that enumeration. dsh-code-index README · Using it：In a workspace session, ask the agent:

- "Which repo are we in — run code_map first."
- "Find every function whose name contains `parse` and where it lives."
- "List the exported symbols in src/core."
- "Rebuild the code index."
- "What changed in the working tree, who calls it, and which tests are likely affected?"
- "Fix duplicate configuration loading during startup." (the router selects the smallest useful context automatically)
dsh-code-index README · Using it：No API key is needed to *index*; the model must of course be configured to call the tools.
dsh-code-index README · More capabilities：The index builds lazily on first use; later calls are served from the on-disk cache with mtime-incremental refresh.
dsh-code-index README · Call graph：`code_refs` traces definitions, callers, and callees. The following is an earlier real example of that existing tool, not a v0.9 Context Card:

dsh-code-index README · Change-aware context：`code_change_context` defaults to the current Git working tree against `HEAD`. It also accepts an inline unified diff, repo-relative `files`, or stable `symbols` IDs. Results are bounded and each inferred relationship carries a provenance label: `exact`, `import-scoped`, or `name-only`. Deletions and renames use the baseline ref when available; untracked non-ignored files are included in working-tree mode.

dsh-code-index README · Edit-ready Context Packs：`code_context` routes change, symbol, architecture, test, exploration, and ambiguous tasks. Deterministic camel/snake terms plus file/path/signature terms rank candidates; exact named symbols are retained before selection. Strong primary seeds find likely tests even on a clean tree. Graph neighborhoods are bounded. BM25 is not used.

dsh-code-index README · Edit-ready Context Packs：`budgetChars` defaults to 5000 and is normalized to 300–20000; `maxFiles` defaults to 12 and `maxSymbols` to 10. Budget units are JavaScript string characters, not tokens or UTF-8 bytes. Both rendered text and serialized final pack must fit. Code is never cut mid-line to fill the cap. Very small budgets can leave only signatures or gaps; a repository identity that cannot fit produces an explicit error. Task display is summarized to 120 characters without affecting routing.

dsh-code-index README · Edit-ready Context Packs：The default canonical return remains a **string**. Request `outputFormat: "pack"` explicitly for the exported `ContextPack` DTO. Its `items` are already selected, with source `file/startLine/endLine/side/ref/mode/code`, `reason`, and separate relationship `resolution/provenance` where relevant. `budget.usedChars` accounts for text; `budget.packChars` accounts for serialized JSON. Render with `renderContextPack`; no hidden candidate list is exposed through the result.

dsh-code-index README · Edit-ready Context Packs：Git changes with a readable, frozen baseline commit classify declarations as added/modified/deleted. Reliable file renames remain supported. Unknown or ambiguous structural identity is `unclassified`; symbol renames are not guessed. Explicit `files`/`symbols` in `code_change_context` remain selection modes, not a proof of a Git modification.

dsh-code-index README · Configuration：Options are passed as the plugin row's `config` in the profile patch (or defaults are used if absent):

```yaml

dsh-code-index README · $DSH_HOME/profiles/<name>/cordis.patch.yml — a bare row overrides by id.：- id: code-index
  config:
    excludeDirs: [generated, playground]
    mapTopFiles: 30
    mapMaxChars: 4000
    autoInject: true
    toolSurface: full
```

dsh-code-index README · $DSH_HOME/profiles/<name>/cordis.patch.yml — a bare row overrides by id.：| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `excludeDirs` | `[]` | Extra directory names appended to built-in excludes. Matching is by exact path component; glob patterns such as `secrets/**` are not supported. |
| `mapTopFiles` | `24` | Max files in a ranked map |
| `mapMaxChars` | `3200` | Hard cap on rendered map characters |
| `mapTtlMs` | `60000` | Refresh interval for the auto-injected map (ms, min 1000) |
| `autoInject` | `true` | Register the system prompt section |
| `codeHealth` | `false` | Register the `code_health` tool (cycles / orphan modules) |
| `toolSurface` | `full` | Experimental `compact` mode exposes `code_index`, `code_context`, and enabled `code_health`; `full` preserves all tools |
| `externalWatch` | `true` | Watch source files in active project contexts for external edits |
| `watchDebounceMs` | `120` | Coalesce watcher events before refreshing affected files (minimum 20 ms) |

text: dsh-code-index README · Supported languages：ArkTS, TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, Go, Rust, Java, C++ and C (`.ets .ts .tsx .mts .cts .js .jsx .mjs .cjs .py .pyi .go .rs .java .cpp .cc .cxx .c++ .hpp .hxx .hh .h .ipp .tpp .inl .c`) via tree-sitter WASM — pure parsing, no native build. The symbol provider seam (`src/extract.ts` + grammars) is where other languages/embeddings plug in later. C/C++ symbol extraction resolves names through the declarator chain (templates, qualified `ns::name` definitions, in-class methods), and `#include "…"` specifiers feed the repo-map reference graph.

dsh-code-index README · ArkTS scope and limits：- Components declared with `struct` appear as `kind: class`, signature `struct Name`.
  Methods, fields, global functions, classes/interfaces/types/enums and module
  variables have stable qualified IDs, owners and source line ranges. Decorators
  (`@Component`, `@ComponentV2`, `@State`, `@Local`, `@Builder`, etc.) are retained
  as metadata and included in the definition's source range.
- `build()` and nested declarative UI blocks parse as ArkTS. Local components and
  explicit ETS/TS imports feed symbols, search, map, references, change context
  and Context Packs. `@Extend` metadata and UI attribute chains are excluded from
  call relationships. Bare capitalized calls in UI bodies have no global-name or
  imported-module fallback; unbound SDK components cannot acquire unrelated
  same-named project targets. Ordinary callback/business calls retain existing
  provenance. `code_refs` uses binding-aware candidates for ArkTS call sites.
- Relative mixed ETS/TS imports work when the target is statically unique.
  Extensionless stems with both ETS and another source file stay unresolved.
  Default imports remain `import-scoped`; no HAR/oh-

dsh-code-index README · How it works：- **Index build** (`src/buildIndex.ts`): recursive scan (excludes applied), per-file tree-sitter extraction (`src/extract.ts`), JSON cache under `<repo>/.dsh-code-index/`, incremental refresh by mtime (only touched files re-parse).
- **Search** (`src/search.ts`): pure scoring — exact `1` / prefix `0.8` / substring `0.5`, export boost, name order tiebreak.
- **Repo map** (`src/repomap.ts`): personalized PageRank over the import graph (teleport = per-file density share, so hub files that are themselves imported by other hubs rise above flat in-degree counting), seeded by the density-aware file score (class/interface/function weighted, test paths damped), top-N files, per-file symbol cap, hard char truncation.
- **Call graph** (`src/refgraph.ts`): call sites extracted per file (per language, with their enclosing function) are resolved by name into callers and callees — `code_refs` exposes this directly, and `code_search` uses call fan-in as a ranking tie-break.
- **Change context** (`src/change-context.ts`): maps Git hunks to stable symbols, then follows bounded provenance-labeled callers, import dependents, entry paths, impact, and likely affected

dsh-code-index README · Known limitations：- **web-tree-sitter pinned to `^0.25` (ESM)** — the 0.25 line uses ESM named exports (`Language`/`Query`); this pairing with `tree-sitter-wasms` static builds is verified working under Node ≥ 22/24.
- Auto-injected maps use DSH's system-prompt assembly context for the active session. Agentless assembly falls back to the DSH process working directory. A newly accessed project may have an empty map on its first prompt while indexing completes; following assemblies receive its map.
- The watcher starts only for projects accessed by a tool and is disposed with the plugin. With `externalWatch: false`, per-call metadata scans still detect ordinary mtime changes.
- Large monorepos still require a directory metadata scan on each tool call. File parsing is incremental, but scan latency depends on repository size and storage speed.
- Function-local variables are excluded. Module declarations and class members are indexed; a parser/graph is not a type checker.
- Source reads reject files changed after the index snapshot, paths resolving outside the root, and current files over 1 MB. Signature-only fallbacks and gaps identify missing evidence; likely t

dsh-code-index README · Development：The benchmark harness under `bench/` compares stock DSH, the published 0.5 baseline, the v0.6 change-aware treatment, and the v0.7 task-aware treatment. It records task completion, input tokens, tool calls, turns, and wall time; it does not invent missing provider usage. The repository contains infrastructure and sample tasks, not measured performance claims.

dsh-code-index README · Development：**WSL → Windows checkouts:** running `pnpm install` from WSL against a checkout on `/mnt/c` leaves Linux-style symlinks that Windows Node cannot traverse (`Cannot find package 'web-tree-sitter'`, `EACCES`). Repair without a reinstall from the Windows side:

```sh
node.exe scripts\fix-wsl-links.mjs            # this repo's node_modules
node.exe scripts\fix-wsl-links.mjs C:\Users\you\.dsh\profiles\web   # a dsh profile install
```
dsh-code-index README · Development：It re-points every dead link at its real `.pnpm` store entry as a junction; safe to re-run (idempotent, reports `fixed: 0` when clean).
